note: Runtime DDL in cloudflare-worker/src that check-runtime-schema-declared.mjs records rather than fails. `refused` lists objects a runtime CREATE names that no migration declares and that SQLite refuses on the fresh build; each entry is re-proved on every run, so the day a refusal stops (a column added, a quote fixed) the entry fails as `refusal-changed` and the object must be declared or its statement deleted. `opaque` counts statements per file that the check cannot expand, each read by hand. `columns` lists columns a runtime ADD COLUMN adds to the fresh build, keyed table.column with the declared type it adds; each is a gap waiting on its migration, re-proved on every run, and stale the moment a migration declares it (D359). The check refuses stale entries in both directions: a ledger of known gaps is only worth reading if every line is still true (D235).

cloudflare-worker/src/util/usersRoleRebu.reason: The atomic rebuild of users under its own name, in one batch: copy to a temporary table, DROP users, re-create users from a DDL string built at runtime, copy back, drop the temporary table. The temporary name exists only inside the batch and users exists before and after it, so the rebuild changes a column constraint, never the set of object names step 9 compares.
